title: High-Temperature Superconductivity of the Fe-Se-H compound
authors: S. I. Bondarenko, A. A. Prokhorov, N. N. Galtsov, V. P. Timofeev, V. P. Koverya, I. S. Bondarenko, A. V. Krevsun
abstract: Using an EPR spectrometer, the dependences of microwave power absorption on magnetic field up to 6000 Oe were measured at temperatures of 3.6-25 K and 295 K in a powdered compound Fe-Se-H, obtained by thermal diffusion of hydrogen into a FeSe single crystal with a critical temperature of 8 K. The shape of the dependences and the analysis of the measurement results confirm the superconductivity of the Fe-Se-H compound at normal pressure, both at temperatures of 3.6-25 K and at 295 K, i.e., at room temperature.
summary: This experimental study investigates the superconducting properties of the $	ext{Fe-Se-H}$ compound using EPR spectroscopy. By measuring magnetic field dependence at room temperature (295 K), the authors provide evidence for superconductivity and extrapolate the critical temperature to significantly higher values. The findings are significant for materials science due to the potential for room-temperature superconductivity.
main_problem: The primary goal is to establish evidence for high-temperature superconductivity in the Fe-Se-H compound, aiming to increase the critical temperature ($T_c$) towards room temperature at normal pressure.
main_result: The $	ext{Fe-Se-H}$ compound exhibits superconductivity at normal pressure, confirmed by characteristic U-shaped magnetic-field dependences and quasi-periodic EPR signals observed up to 295 K.
method: The study utilizes Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) spectroscopy to measure the dependence of microwave power absorption on magnetic field and temperature.
model_or_system: The physical system is the $	ext{Fe-Se-H}$ compound, formed by hydrogen diffusion into an $	ext{FeSe}$ single crystal. Measurements are performed on both powdered and single-crystal samples.
key_observables: The derivative of microwave power absorption ($	ext{dP/dH}$), U-shaped magnetic-field dependences (MFDS), and quasi-periodic oscillations in the EPR signal.
important_parameters: Temperatures ranging from 3.6 K to 295 K; magnetic fields up to 6000 Oe; the calculated critical temperature extrapolation suggests $T_c \approx 340 	ext{ K}$.
main_assumptions: The quasi-periodic variations in the EPR signal are attributed to the presence of Abrikosov vortices, and the vortex area is approximated by $S_0 \approx \pi [\lambda(T)]^2/4$.
figures_summary: Figures show the U-shaped MFDS for both the single crystal $	ext{FeSe}$ and the $	ext{Fe-Se-H}$ powder at various temperatures, and high-resolution EPR signals demonstrating quasi-periodicity.
paper_structure: The paper presents measurements of microwave power absorption using EPR spectroscopy on $	ext{Fe-Se-H}$ across a wide temperature range. Evidence for superconductivity is drawn from the U-shaped MFDS and the analysis of quasi-periodic signals, leading to an extrapolation of the critical temperature.
why_interesting: The work directly addresses high-$T_c$ superconductivity, a major topic in condensed matter physics, using advanced spectroscopic techniques to probe superconducting vortex dynamics.
